Best next steps are to improve exposure of the hepatocystic triangle, continue focused dissection there, and keep the camera stable unless needed for better view of the gallbladder neck and lower-third liver bed.

The strongest signal is persistent partial exposure of Calot's triangle with residual fat/fibrous tissue and only one convincing tubular structure entering the gallbladder; the second structure is not confidently separable, and the lower-third gallbladder-liver interface does not show a clear detached cystic plate.
